question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{x} - 10.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{x} - 10 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{y} - 10. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{y} - 10\\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{y} & = x + 10\\[5pt] \sqrt{y} & = \dfrac32 (x + 10)\\[5pt] (\sqrt{y})^2 & = \left( \dfrac32 (x + 10) \right)^2\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac94 (x + 10)^2 \\[5pt] \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac94 (x + 10)^2}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \geq 0, \qquad f(x) \geq -10. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \geq -10, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \geq 0. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = 5\sqrt[3]{x} + 3.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 5\sqrt[3]{x} + 3 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 5\sqrt[3]{y} + 3. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 5\sqrt[3]{y} + 3 \\[5pt] 5 \sqrt[3]{y} & = x - 3\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y} & = \dfrac 1 5 (x - 3)\\[5pt] \big(\sqrt[3]{y}\big)^3 & = \left (\dfrac 1 5 (x - 3) \right)^3\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac 1 {125} (x - 3)^3 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac 1 {125} (x - 3)^3}. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = 6 - 4\sqrt x.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 6 - 4\sqrt x \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 6 - 4\sqrt y. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 6 - 4\sqrt y\\[5pt] 4\sqrt{y} & = 6 - x\\[5pt] \sqrt{y} & =\dfrac 1 4 (6 - x)\\[5pt] (\sqrt{y})^2 & = \left( \dfrac 1 4 (6 - x) \right)^2\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac 1 {16} (6 - x)^2 \\[5pt] \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac 1 {16} (6 - x)^2}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \geq 0, \qquad f(x) \leq 6. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \leq 6, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \geq 0. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Radical Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$

\[ y = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{x}} - 1 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

\[ x = \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{y}} - 1. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

\begin{align} x &= \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{y}} - 1 \\[5pt] x + 1 &= \dfrac{3}{\sqrt{y}} \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{x + 1} &= \dfrac{\sqrt{y}}{3} \\[5pt] \sqrt{y} &= \dfrac{3}{x + 1} \\[5pt] (\sqrt{y})^2 &= \left(\dfrac{3}{x + 1}\right)^2 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{9}{(x + 1)^2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is

\[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{9}{(x+1)^2}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are given by \[ x > 0, \qquad f(x) > -1. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x > -1, \qquad f^{-1}(x) > 0. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{x}} + 1.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{x}} + 1 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{y}} + 1. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac {2} {5\sqrt{y}} + 1\\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{5\sqrt{y}} & = x - 1\\[5pt] \sqrt{y} &= \dfrac{2}{5 (x - 1)} \\[5pt] \left(\sqrt{y}\right)^2 &= \left( \dfrac{2}{5 (x - 1)} \right)^2 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{4}{25 (x - 1)^2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{4} {25 (x - 1)^2}}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x > 0, \qquad f(x) > 1. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x > 1, \qquad f^{-1}(x) > 0. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Reciprocal Radical Function

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 3 - \dfrac{4}{\sqrt[3]{x}} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 3 - \dfrac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows: \begin{align} x & = 3 - \dfrac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}}\\[5pt] x - 3& = -\dfrac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}}\\[5pt] 3 - x & = \dfrac{4}{\sqrt[3]{y}}\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{3 - x} & = \dfrac{\sqrt[3]{y}}{4}\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y} & = \dfrac{4}{3 - x} \\[5pt] (\sqrt[3]{y})^3 & = \left( \dfrac{4}{3 - x} \right)^3 \\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{64}{(3 - x)^3} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{64}{(3 - x)^3}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \neq 0, \qquad f(x) \neq 3. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \neq 3, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \neq 0. \]

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = 2 - \dfrac {1} {6 \sqrt{x}}.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 2 - \dfrac {1} {6 \sqrt{x}} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 2 - \dfrac {1} {6 \sqrt{y}}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 2 - \dfrac {1} {6 \sqrt{y}} \\[5pt] \dfrac {1} {6 \sqrt{y}} & = 2 - x \\[5pt] \sqrt{y} &= \dfrac{1} {6 (2 - x)} \\[5pt] \left(\sqrt{y}\right)^2 &= \left( \dfrac{1} {6 (2 - x)} \right)^2 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{1}{36 (2 - x)^2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{1}{36 (2 - x)^2} }. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x > 0, \qquad f(x) < 2. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x < 2, \qquad f^{-1}(x) > 0. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 2\sqrt[3]{3x - 1} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 2\sqrt[3]{3y - 1}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

\begin{align} x & = 2\sqrt[3]{3y - 1}\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{3y - 1} & = \dfrac{1}{2}x\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{3y - 1} \right)^3 & = \left( \dfrac{1}{2}x \right)^3\\[5pt] 3y - 1 & = \dfrac{1}{8}x^3 \\[5pt] 3y & = \dfrac{1}{8}x^3 + 1\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{1}{3}\left(\dfrac{1}{8}x^3 + 1\right)\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{1}{24}\left(x^3 + 8\right) \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{24}\left(x^3 + 8\right). \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.text: Find the inverse of the function $f(x) = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[3] {2x - 1}} + 2.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[3] {2x - 1}} + 2 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[3] {2 y - 1}} + 2. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac {3} {\sqrt[3] {2y - 1}} + 2 \\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{2y - 1} & = \dfrac{3} {x - 2} \\[5pt] (\sqrt[3]{2y - 1})^3 & = \left( \dfrac 3 {x - 2} \right)^3\\[5pt] 2y - 1 &= \dfrac{27}{(x - 2)^3} \\[5pt] 2y &= \dfrac{27}{(x - 2)^3} + 1 \\[5pt] y &= \dfrac{27} {2(x - 2)^3} + \dfrac {1} {2} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) =\bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ \dfrac{27} {2(x - 2)^3} + \dfrac {1} {2}}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \neq \dfrac 1 2, \qquad f(x) \neq 2. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \neq 2, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \neq \dfrac 1 2. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{x - 3} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{y - 3}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

\begin{align} x & = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{y - 3}\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{y - 3} & = 3x\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{y - 3} \right)^3 & = \left( 3x \right)^3\\[5pt] y - 3 & = 27x^3 \\[5pt] y & = 27x^3 + 3 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = 27x^3 + 3. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{x - 1} + 3 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{y - 1} + 3. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows:

\begin{align} x & = \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{y - 1} + 3\\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{2}\sqrt{y - 1} & = x - 3\\[5pt] \sqrt{y - 1} & = 2(x - 3)\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt{y - 1} \right)^2 & = \left( 2(x - 3) \right)^2\\[5pt] y - 1 & = 4(x - 3)^2 \\[5pt] y & = 4(x - 3)^2 + 1 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = 4(x - 3)^2 + 1. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \geq 1, \qquad f(x) \geq 3. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \geq 3, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \geq 1. \]

example.title: Finding the Inverse of a Radical Function Containing a Linear Argument

question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = 2 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3x + 2}} \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = 2 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3y + 2}}. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = 2 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3y + 2}}\\[5pt] x - 2 & = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3y + 2}}\\[5pt] 2 - x & = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3y + 2}}\\[5pt] \sqrt{3y + 2} & = \dfrac{1}{2 - x}\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt{3y + 2} \right)^2 & = \left( \dfrac{1}{2 - x} \right)^2\\[5pt] 3y + 2 & = \dfrac{1}{(x-2)^2}\\[5pt] 3y & = \dfrac{1}{(x-2)^2} - 2\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{1}{3(x-2)^2} - \dfrac{2}{3} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{3(x-2)^2} - \dfrac{2}{3}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \gt -\dfrac{2}{3}, \qquad f(x) \lt 2. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \lt 2, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \gt -\dfrac{2}{3}. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text:
The function $f(x),$ defined as \[ f(x) = \dfrac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6x - 1}} + 2, \qquad x \neq \dfrac{1}{6} \] has an inverse function given by \[f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4}{81 (x - 2)^3} + \dfrac{1}{6}, \qquad x \neq 2.\]

What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6x - 1}} + 2 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6 y - 1}} + 2. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6 y - 1}} + 2\\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{k\sqrt[3]{6 y - 1}} & = x - 2\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{6 y - 1} & = \dfrac{2} {k (x - 2)}\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{6 y - 1} \right)^3 & = \left( \dfrac{2}{k (x - 2)} \right)^3 \\[5pt] 6 y - 1 & = \dfrac{2^3}{k^3 (x - 2)^3}\\[5pt] 6 y & = \dfrac{8}{k^3 (x - 2)^3} + 1\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{4}{3 k ^3 (x - 2)^3} + \dfrac 1 6 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{4}{3 k ^3 (x - 2)^3} + \dfrac 1 6 , \qquad x \neq 2. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ \dfrac{4}{3 k^3} = \dfrac{4}{81} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{3}. \]

example.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text:
The function $f(x),$ defined as \[ f(x) = \dfrac {k} {\sqrt{8 x + 3 }} + 2,\qquad x \gt -\dfrac{3}{8} \] has an inverse function given by \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{9}{2 (x - 2)^2} - \dfrac{3}{8}, \qquad x \gt 2. \]

What is the value of $k?$ Assume that $k>0.$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac {k} {\sqrt{8 x + 3 }} + 2 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac {k} {\sqrt{8 y + 3 }} + 2. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{k} {\sqrt{8 y + 3 }} + 2\\[5pt] x - 2 & = \dfrac{k} {\sqrt{8 y + 3 }} \\[5pt] \sqrt{8 y + 3} & = \dfrac{k} {x - 2}\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt{8 y + 3} \right)^2 & = \left( \dfrac{k} {x - 2} \right)^2 \\[5pt] 8 y + 3 & = \dfrac{k^2} {(x - 2)^2}\\[5pt] 8 y & = \dfrac{k^2}{(x - 2)^2} - 3\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{k^2}{8 (x - 2)^2} - \dfrac{3}{8} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{k^2}{8 (x - 2)^2} - \dfrac{3}{8}, \qquad x \gt 2. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ \dfrac{k^2}{8} = \dfrac{9}{2} \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{ 6}. \]

question.text: The function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt{x - 5} + 6$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = 16(x - 6)^2 + 5.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt{x - 5} + 6 \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt{y - 5} + 6. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt{y - 5} + 6 \\[5pt] \dfrac{1}{k} \sqrt{y - 5} & = x - 6\\[5pt] \sqrt{y - 5} & = k(x - 6)\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt{y - 5} \right)^2 & = \left( k (x - 6) \right)^2\\[5pt] y - 5 & = k^2 (x - 6)^2\\[5pt] y & = k^2 (x - 6)^2 + 5 \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = k^2 (x - 6)^2 + 5. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ k^2 = 16 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{4}. \]

Note: The domain and range of $f(x)$ are \[ x \geq 5, \qquad f(x) \geq 6. \]

Therefore, the domain and range of $f^{-1}(x)$ are \[ x \geq 6, \qquad f^{-1}(x) \geq 5. \]

example.title: Determining an Unknown Value Given the Inverse of a Radical Function

question.text: The function $f(x) = \sqrt[3]{3x + 1} + k$ has an inverse function given by $f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}(x+4)^3 - \dfrac{1}{3}.$ What is the value of $k?$
question.explanation:
To find $f^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y{:}$ \[ y = \sqrt[3]{3x + 1} + k \]

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives \[ x = \sqrt[3]{3y+ 1} + k. \]

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation as follows: \begin{align} x & = \sqrt[3]{3y+ 1} + k\\[5pt] \sqrt[3]{3y + 1} & = x - k\\[5pt] \left( \sqrt[3]{3y + 1} \right)^3 & = \left( x-k \right)^3\\[5pt] 3y + 1 & = (x-k)^3\\[5pt] 3y & = (x-k)^3 - 1\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{1}{3}(x-k)^3 - \dfrac{1}{3} \end{align}

Therefore, the inverse function is \[ f^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{1}{3}(x-k)^3 - \dfrac{1}{3}. \]

Comparing our answer with the given expression, we conclude that \[ -k = 4 \qquad \Longrightarrow \qquad k = -4. \]
